panels.description: Node means graph nodes; leaf means source diagnostics. Their counts must not be added to infer unique faults.

panels.description: Receive freshness, discovered publishers, current rates and exporter totals for every configured topic. Counts include decode failures; age refers to the latest valid decoded message. Retained notifications do not expire by age.

panels.title: Reported boundary snapshot

panels.description: Seconds in each source clock, including pose/twist/accel stamps. Not necessarily Unix time; no difference from wall time is computed.
panels.title: Source ROS timestamps

panels.description: All current graph paths, including OK. These are diagnostic graph nodes, not a count of unique dead processes.
panels.title: All reported diagnostic paths

panels.description: Exporter build version, source revision, and Go toolchain version. The metric has value 1; labels contain the information. Different binaries can expose different runtime metric sets.
panels.title: Exporter build

panels.description: Wall-clock time since the Autoware exporter process started; resets on restart. This is not vehicle or ROS uptime.
panels.title: Process uptime

panels.description: Go runtime version from go_info. The metric value is always 1; the version is carried in a label. Go/runtime panels require the standard Go collector metrics.
panels.title: Go runtime

panels.description: Wall-clock duration of the complete Prometheus scrape, including response transfer and processing. Autoware exporter does not expose a separate collection duration.
panels.title: Prometheus scrape duration

panels.description: CPU time consumed per wall-clock second, in CPU cores. A value of 1 means one fully utilized logical CPU; a multithreaded process can exceed 1. Rates use Grafana's rate interval and require multiple samples.
panels.title: CPU usage

panels.description: Resident memory is physical memory currently resident for the exporter process. Virtual memory is its mapped address space and can be much larger; the two are not interchangeable measures of memory pressure.
panels.title: Process memory

panels.description: Goroutines are Go tasks, OS threads are runtime threads, and GOMAXPROCS limits simultaneous execution of Go code. They measure different aspects of concurrency and need not match.
panels.title: Go concurrency

panels.description: Samples scraped before and after metric relabeling, plus series newly added during a scrape. New-series counts are per scrape, not the total number of active series. Changes can reflect actor churn or label changes.
panels.title: Scrape samples

panels.description: Open file descriptors compared with the process limit. The limit uses the right-hand axis so the open count remains readable; compare numeric values rather than the apparent line heights.
panels.title: Open file descriptors

panels.description: Receive/transmit rates from the process network-namespace counters. Scope depends on deployment: with host networking they include host traffic; in a private container network namespace they include that namespace. These are not exporter-only application bytes.
panels.title: Network namespace traffic

panels.description: Exported GC pause quantiles describe the runtime summary, not percentiles calculated over the selected dashboard range. Mean pause is rate(sum) / rate(count) over Grafana's rate interval. It can be unavailable when there are no GC events.
panels.title: GC pause duration

panels.description: Heap alloc is bytes in allocated objects; inuse is heap spans in use; idle is unused spans; released is idle memory returned to the OS; sys is heap memory obtained from the OS. These overlap and must not be summed.
panels.title: Heap memory

panels.description: Allocated object memory, total memory obtained from the OS by the Go runtime, and the next GC heap target. Reserved runtime memory is not the same as process RSS or a container memory limit.
panels.title: Memory allocator

panels.description: Rate of cumulative bytes allocated by the Go runtime, including allocations that have already been freed. This is allocation throughput, not net memory growth.
panels.title: Allocation rate

panels.description: Rates of heap object allocations and frees. Differences indicate changes in live object count over the measurement interval, not necessarily a leak.
panels.title: Object allocation & frees

panels.description: Number of allocated heap objects currently tracked by the Go runtime. Use its trend together with allocation rates and heap memory to investigate retention.
panels.title: Heap objects

panels.description: Rate of completed garbage collections, in collections per second. A period without GC can produce zero; absent metrics or insufficient samples produce no data.
panels.title: Garbage collections

panels.description: Wall-clock time since the most recent garbage collection. This calculation depends on host clock time. A longer interval can simply mean low allocation activity.
panels.title: Time since last GC

panels.description: Stack memory in use versus memory obtained from the OS for stacks. These are Go runtime stack metrics, not the process virtual address-space size.
panels.title: Stack memory

panels.description: Runtime bookkeeping memory for profiling hash buckets, GC metadata, allocator caches, spans, and other allocations. Some values are in-use memory and others are reserved; they overlap and are not an additive total.
panels.title: Runtime metadata memory

panels.description: Configured GOGC percentage: the GC heap growth target relative to the live heap after the previous collection. This is a tuning setting, not the fraction of time spent in GC.
panels.title: GC target

panels.description: Go runtime soft memory limit (GOMEMLIMIT). Unlimited denotes the runtime's effectively unbounded default. It is not a hard process or container limit and does not cover all memory outside the Go runtime.
panels.title: Go memory limit

panels.description: Maximum virtual memory address-space limit exposed by the process collector. Unlimited denotes an effectively unbounded limit. This is not a resident-memory or container-memory limit.
panels.title: Virtual memory limit

list.label: Datasource
list.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
list.description: Prometheus datasource containing Autoware exporter metrics. Set its scrape interval to match the Prometheus job.

list.label: Job
list.name: job
list.description: Scrape jobs discovered from autoware_exporter_build_info; no job name is prescribed. All expands only the discovered jobs.

list.label: Instance
list.name: instance
list.description: Exporter targets discovered from the selected jobs. Instances remain separate in queries and legends.

list.label: Vehicles
list.name: vehicle
list.description: Vehicle names discovered from the selected exporter targets; no fixed vehicle names or count are required.
